subject: Procurement route decision — PO vs marketplace (HelioHealth)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up: procurement routes & AWS Marketplace option

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our end so we can align on the procurement route (PO vs card) and marketplace option: 

Recap from today's discovery call:
- Primary objective: a 6–8 week pilot (50 devices, API calls for inference) to validate latency and cost for an interactive triage assistant.
- Compliance: SSO + SCIM required; SOC2 evidence requested by procurement.
- Buying preference: procurement team indicated preference for PO but pilot team wants minimal friction to start.
- Cloud preference: core infra on AWS, but legal asked if GCP/Azure options exist for contract scope.

Options we discussed: 
1) Direct invoice / PO (Standard enterprise flow) — full contract, standard T&Cs, 30–60 day payment terms. Best for long-term procurement and reserved capacity.
2) Credit card (self-serve) — fastest to start but not acceptable for enterprise-wide commitments. Good for dev/trial accounts.
3) AWS Marketplace (procurement via marketplace) — faster procurement cadence than PO for trials, can centralize billing, and often reduces legal review scope; pricing and metering handled through AWS.

Attachments I’m sharing: pricing_summary.pdf (pilot-level pricing + reserved options) and redwood-sso-evidence.pdf (SSO/SCIM + SOC2 excerpt).

Requested next steps / asks: 
- Can you confirm whether procurement is open to an AWS Marketplace trial for the pilot? That would let you start within days while we finalize a PO for production.
- If PO is the only acceptable path, please share the procurement contact and typical PO timeline (30/45/60 days).
- Any contractual must-haves (data residency, additional clauses) we should surface now?

Proposed milestone-based plan if you want to proceed with Marketplace-first: 
- Week 0: onboarding via Marketplace (card or Marketplace procurement), provision pilot environment.
- Week 1–4: pilot run + performance/quality checks.
- Week 3: commercial sync — decide reserved capacity or move to PO for production.

I can loop in Marissa (cc'd) to pull together a short statement of work and draft quote once you confirm the procurement route.

Thanks — available tomorrow 10–12 PT if you want a 20-minute cadence to align with procurement.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: pricing_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages); redwood-sso-evidence.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

From: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@heliohealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: J. Miller <jmiller@heliohealth.com>, procurement@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: procurement routes & AWS Marketplace option

Thanks Ben — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement preference: long term, we absolutely go with PO. That said, procurement team (cc'd) said they're open to an AWS Marketplace trial for the pilot if the legal review is smaller and billing flows through Marketplace. That would let the product team start testing next week.
- Cloud preference: AWS is primary; however, our infra team asked if Redwood supports GCP or Azure images in case we want cross-cloud redundancy later. Can you confirm model parity across clouds?
- Timeline: procurement estimates ~45 days for PO approval for a production contract. For the pilot, Marketplace would be ideal to compress the start time to under a week.

Action items on our side: 
- I will confirm with procurement whether they require any additional security artifacts beyond the SOC2 excerpt (i.e., firewall diagrams, encryption key management).
- J. Miller (IT Ops) will share a brief network diagram and the person who manages the billing relationship.

Ask of Redwood:
- If we go Marketplace-first, can you provide a short MOP (minimal onboarding playbook) and a Marketplace SKU or link?
- If PO is needed immediately, please share standard PO instructions and a template invoice address for HelioHealth.

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement + IT — Tuesday 8/22 PT works for us (we're flexible).

Best,
Alyssa Park
Product Lead, HelioHealth
alyssa.park@heliohealth.com

Hi Alyssa — great, thanks for confirming procurement is open to a Marketplace pilot. A few concrete items from our side to keep momentum: 

1) Marketplace onboarding: I'll send the AWS Marketplace SKU and one-click onboarding link to you in a separate note by end of day. That will allow your product team to spin up the pilot immediately.
2) MOP & SOW: Marissa (cc'd) will draft a one-page MOP for pilot success criteria and a short SOW we can sign digitally. Expect those in the next 48 hours.
3) PO path: For production, our legal/commercial team typically accepts HelioHealth PO with standard Redwood terms. To speed review, please send any non-standard contract language procurement requires (data residency, indemnity cap changes).
4) Cloud parity: Vivek — can you confirm model parity across AWS/GCP/Azure? If there's any functional delta we should call it out now so Alyssa's infra team can decide.

Proposed mutual action plan: 
- Day 0: Marketplace onboarding (pilot account provisioned)
- Day 7–30: Pilot + weekly sync (metrics: latency P95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy on sample prompts)
- Day 21: Commercial check-in; confirm production sizing and whether PO is required for reserved capacity

Related links: HubSpot deal attached here for internal tracking (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567). I'll also prepare a DocuSign quote (HHL-2026-07) if you want a standing estimate to attach to the PO.

If helpful, I'm free tomorrow 10–11 PT for a 15-minute alignment with procurement and IT.

Thanks,
Ben

Hi Alyssa — looping in the commercial side. Per Ben's notes, attached is a pilot quote (HHL-Quote-Redwood.xlsx) and a short SOW outline. Key commercial notes: 

- Pilot pricing: metered usage for the trial, capped at an agreed not-to-exceed amount.
- Reserved capacity/production: 12-month commitment options with discounted unit pricing.
- Marketplace delta: if you purchase via AWS Marketplace, invoice and payment flow through AWS; contract crossing (entitlement) may require a separate PO for reserved capacity later.

Next steps we suggest: 
1) Alyssa/procurement: confirm whether Marketplace onboarding is acceptable for the pilot this week.
2) If yes — we'll prepare a DocuSign quote for signature and send the Marketplace SKU + onboarding playbook.
